chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, he narrated, saying:

When Al-Mu'tassim was poisoned, he made a vow that if he was cured, he would give much wealth in charity. When he was cured, he asked the jurists about the definition of 'much wealth', and they differed regarding it. Some said one hundred thousand, and some said ten thousand, and they offered various differing opinions regarding it, so the matter became confused for him.

Then a man from his companions, called Suf'wan, said to him: 'Why do you not send to this Aswad and ask him about it?' Al-Mu'tassim said to him: 'Who do you mean, woe to you?' He said: 'Ibn al-Rida.' He said to him: 'Does he know anything about this?'
He said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, if he extracts you from this confusion, then so-and-so is due upon me; otherwise, strike me with one hundred strikes.'

Al-Mu'tassim said: 'I am pleased, O Ja'far ibn Muhammad. Go to him and ask him about the definition of much wealth.' So Ja'far went to Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) and asked him about the definition of much wealth.
He said to him: 'The much is eighty.'
Ja'far said to him: 'O my master, I think he will ask me for the reason behind it.'
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Majestic, says: "Allah gave you victory in many places." So we counted those places, and they were eighty places.'

key_terms.ابْنُ الرَّضَا: Ibn al-Rida (a title for the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'much wealth' for charity according to Imam Ali al-Rida (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Abbasid court's reliance on the Ahl al-Bayt for resolving jurisprudential ambiguities, specifically regarding the definition of 'excessive wealth' (al-mal al-kathir) for vows. Imam Ali al-Rida (AS) provides a numerological derivation from Surah Al-Anfal (8:7), linking the Arabic word 'mawatin' (places) to the number eighty, thereby establishing a precise legal standard through divine revelation. This narrative highlights the unique Shia scholarly method of extracting legal rulings from the linguistic nuances of the Quran.
